journeys.title: Big Cats of India
journeys.description: A rare, four-week odyssey through India’s most powerful wilderness realms, one of the only places on Earth where such an extraordinary constellation of big cats can be.
journeys.intro:
A rare, four-week odyssey through India’s most powerful wilderness realms, one of the only places on Earth where such an extraordinary constellation of big cats can be experienced in a single, seamless journey. Feel the thin, silent air of the high Himalayas as Snow Leopards move like ghosts across snowbound ridgelines.

Enter ancient forests where Tigers command shadow and light, and enter weathered granite landscapes where Leopards move stealthily. Traverse the sunlit plains that shelter the last Asiatic Lions in their only natural home.

Guided by expert naturalists and supported by effortless logistics, this all-inclusive expedition weaves exceptional wildlife photography, over 400 bird species, and refined wilderness stays into an experience that is intimate, elemental, and profoundly unforgettable.

Explore four distinct wilderness habitats on this immersive four-week journey, tracking Snow Leopards, Bengal Tigers, Asiatic Lions, and Indian Leopards, alongside rich mammalian diversity and over 400 bird species.

Enjoy thoughtfully curated accommodations ranging from intimate boutique lodges to refined luxury retreats, seamless travel with optional company-owned jet transfers, and the flexibility to extend your journey to cultural destinations such as Jaipur, Agra, or Varanasi. This is a fully customisable, all-inclusive safari designed for depth, comfort, and exclusivity.

body: Arrive in India’s bustling capital, where ancient heritage blends with contemporary life. Settle into your hotel, meet your expedition team, and prepare for an unforgettable multi-habitat wildlife journey across India.

Fly into the stark, high-altitude landscapes of Ladakh, the Himalayan kingdom where Snow Leopards reign unseen across rocky ridgelines and frozen valleys. Stay in comfortable mountain lodges and venture out each day with seasoned trackers who scan rugged cliffs for signs of the “Grey Ghost.” Along the way, encounter Himalayan Blue Sheep, Red Foxes, soaring eagles, and the raw silence of the trans-Himalayan wilderness.

Leave the mountains behind for the warm forests of Ranthambhore, one of the world’s premier destinations for Tiger photography. Here, tigers stride past ancient temples and fort walls rising from lakes and forests. Morning and evening safaris carry you through diverse landscapes where sambars graze, crocodiles bask, and birdlife thrives in golden light.

Continue overland to Jawai, a dramatic landscape shaped by volcanic granite where Leopards coexist peacefully with local shepherds. The region’s open terrain and unique rock formations create exceptional photographic conditions. Enjoy tranquil mornings watching leopards emerge from cave dwellings and evenings glowing with pink and amber desert light.

Arrive in Gir, the final refuge of the Asiatic Lion,a species of ancient lineage. Safari through teak forests and open scrublands where these majestic cats roam freely, offering rare and unforgettable encounters. Your journey concludes with a flight back to Delhi, carrying with you memories of India’s four magnificent big-cat domains.

The expedition begins in Delhi, before the world recedes into the high Himalayas of Ladakh. Above 3,500 metres, survival feels elemental. In one of the Snow Leopard’s most critical remaining ranges, where fewer than 7,000 survive globally, tracking becomes an act of deep attention, guided by wind, snow, and stone.

From this silence, the journey descends into Ranthambhore National Park, where Bengal Tigers move through forests shaped by centuries of royal history, ancient forts, and reflective lakes. In Jawai, part of the ancient Aravalli range formed over hundreds of millions of years, Leopards roam freely beyond park boundaries, protected through rare coexistence with the Rabari community.
The journey concludes in Gir National Park, the last refuge of the Asiatic Lion, revived from fewer than 20 individuals a century ago to a population of over 800 today.

Seamless logistics, discreet luxury lodges, and optional private aviation allow for unhurried immersion. Extensions to the Taj Mahal, Jaipur, or Varanasi complete a journey defined by depth, place, and meaning.

journeys.title: Central India’s Six-Park Safari
journeys.description: The tiger is more than an endangered species.
journeys.intro:
The tiger is more than an endangered species. It is an idea, an emotion, a living symbol etched into India’s cultural memory and the imagination of the wild. This expedition is a homage to that presence. Journey into the wild heart of Central India on a seamless overland safari through six extraordinary tiger landscapes.

Bamboo thickets whisper in Tadoba, sal forests in Pench recall stories older than words, and Kanha opens into vast meadows where light drifts like breath across grass. Bandhavgarh rises in stone and shadow, Panna’s rivers carve deep, ancient gorges, and Satpura’s rugged hills fold into forests that feel almost primordial.

body: Journey into the wild heart of Central India on a seamless overland safari through six extraordinary tiger landscapes. Bamboo thickets whisper in Tadoba, sal forests in Pench recall stories older than words, and Kanha opens into vast meadows where light drifts like breath across grass.
Bandhavgarh rises in stone and shadow, Panna’s rivers carve deep, ancient gorges, and Satpura’s rugged hills fold into forests that feel almost primordial.

Throughout the journey, refined wilderness lodges offer quiet refuge, while expert naturalists guide private safaris attuned to patience and intuition. Tigers emerge, leopards linger at the edges of sight, sloth bears shuffle through clearings, wild dogs flash through forests, and birds stitch the skies.
Shaped by rivers, forests, and ancient plateaus, this is not merely a safari, it is an immersion into the living soul of Central India’s wilderness.

This immersive expedition journeys through six legendary tiger reserves, offering exceptional opportunities to photograph tigers, leopards, sloth bears, wild dogs, and more than 300 species of birds across riverine forests, open grasslands, and rugged plateaus.

Seamless overland transfers eliminate the need for internal flights, allowing the landscape to unfold naturally, while carefully chosen luxury lodges provide comfort, exclusivity, and close proximity to the wilderness.

The itinerary may be extended to include cultural icons such as Varanasi, Agra, or Jaipur, or expanded to Gir National Park for Asiatic lions or the Himalayas for snow leopards, creating a fully personalized wildlife-and-culture epic across India.

Arrive in Delhi and prepare for your wildlife journey before traveling onward to Tadoba. Settle into your lodge and experience your first safaris in Maharashtra’s premier tiger reserve, a landscape of forests, meadows, and lakes that support thriving populations of tigers, leopards, sloth bears, and wild dogs.

Spend four days exploring Tadoba’s rich landscapes with multiple private safaris. Its mix of bamboo thickets, open meadows, and waterbodies offers exceptional visibility, making it one of India’s most reliable destinations for tiger sightings.

Travel to Kanha, a jewel of the Central Indian highlands, known for barasingha, gaur, leopards, and tigers moving through its vast sal forests. Continue to Bandhavgarh, renowned for its high tiger density and ancient fort-topped cliffs, where each safari reveals both wildlife and striking terrain.

Enter Panna’s dramatic landscape of sandstone gorges, waterfalls, and the pristine Ken River. Safari by jeep and boat to observe tigers, leopards, crocodiles, raptors, and other fauna thriving in this restored and flourishing habitat.

Conclude your journey in Satpura, a quieter, more intimate wildlife sanctuary characterized by rolling hills, dense forests, and river valleys. Track tigers, leopards, sloth bears, and hyenas through this rugged terrain before departing via Bhopal.

This journey is rooted in landscapes that have actively shaped India’s conservation story. Kanha National Park is inseparable from the pioneering work of George Schaller, whose seminal research on predator-prey dynamics here helped define modern tiger ecology and influenced the birth of Project Tiger.

Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, has risen as a flagship success, its resurgence driven by sustained protection, resilient prey bases, and water-rich forests that now support some of Central India’s most confident tiger populations.

Bandhavgarh National Park carries both drama and legacy: steep cliffs crowned by an ancient fort and legendary tigers such as Charger, Sita, and Bamera, whose stories helped define India’s reputation for intimate tiger encounters.

Panna National Park stands as a powerful conservation testament, once devoid of tigers, it was carefully restored through one of India’s most successful reintroduction programmes, proving how science and stewardship can revive an entire ecosystem.

The journey culminates in Satpura National Park, celebrated in classic Indian natural history writing for its rugged highlands, river systems, and layered habitats, an older, quieter wilderness that reveals the geological depth and diversity of Central India itself.

Together, these landscapes do more than offer sightings; they reveal how terrain, time, and conservation vision have each played a role in shaping one of the most compelling wildlife regions on Earth.

journeys.description: Across western India lie landscapes that feel almost untouched by time , grasslands rippling with antelope, salt deserts shimmering like glass, granite hills concealing.
journeys.intro:
Across western India lie landscapes that feel almost untouched by time , grasslands rippling with antelope, salt deserts shimmering like glass, granite hills concealing secretive leopards, and ancient forests resonant with the calls of lions.

This four-habitat, four-big-cat expedition journeys through India’s wildest frontiers, unfolding from Gir to Velavadar, the Rann of Kutch, Jawai, and the Desert National Park.

Designed for travellers drawn to remote wilderness without compromise, the experience blends dramatic terrain, rare predators, and immersive cultural encounters, all supported by seamless logistics and refined comfort. Journey through four strikingly different landscapes in pursuit of India’s most iconic predators and desert-adapted wildlife.

From the lions of Gir and the leopards of Jawai to the distinctive fauna of Velavadar, the Rann of Kutch, and the Desert National Park, this fully bespoke, all-inclusive expedition reveals the raw drama of western India’s wilderness. Optional travel aboard business jets ensures seamless transitions and refined comfort across vast and contrasting regions.

body: Journey through four strikingly different landscapes in pursuit of India’s most iconic predators and desert-adapted wildlife. From the lions of Gir and the leopards of Jawai to the distinctive fauna of Velavadar, the Rann of Kutch, and the Desert National Park, this fully bespoke, all-inclusive expedition reveals the raw drama of western India’s wilderness.
Optional travel aboard business jets ensures seamless transitions and refined comfort across vast and contrasting regions.

In the rugged teak and acacia forests of Gir, the world’s last Asiatic Lions continue a lineage that once roamed from India to the Mediterranean. Safaris reveal not just lions, but the rhythm of a thriving ecosystem,Jungle Cats slinking through undergrowth, Hyenas trotting across trails, and flocks of birds gathering along seasonal streams. Quiet evenings in your lodge offer a peaceful counterpoint to the day’s excitement.

Velavadar feels like a living canvas,golden grasslands brushed by the wind and dotted with elegant Blackbucks. Here, wolf packs navigate vast open plains, foxes emerge at twilight, and raptors ride warm thermals above. The simplicity of the landscape creates striking photographic compositions and an atmosphere of profound solitude.

The Rann of Kutch introduces an entirely different mood: an endless salt wilderness where the horizon dissolves into shimmering heat. Safaris bring encounters with the rare Asiatic Wild Ass and other desert-adapted wildlife. Dawn and dusk paint the flats in soft pinks and silvers, transforming the desert into a surreal, dreamlike world.

Arriving in Jawai feels like stepping into a mythic realm of stone. Giant granite boulders rise from pastoral plains, forming natural fortresses where leopards thrive. This is a landscape shaped as much by coexistence as geology,Rabari herders move through the terrain with their livestock while leopards watch silently from the rocks.
The resulting harmony offers exceptional opportunities for close yet ethical leopard sightings.

In the Desert National Park, wind-sculpted dunes and thorny scrub create one of India’s most dramatic and fragile ecosystems. Desert Cats slip between shadows, Wolves traverse ridges, and Hyenas work the night. The vastness here is humbling, offering a rare sense of isolation found in few places on earth. After your final explorations, depart carrying the essence of India’s wild frontiers.

Conclude your adventure in Ranthambhore National Park, one of India’s most iconic tiger reserves. Here, the Royal Bengal Tiger roams amidst ancient temples, lakes, and fort ruins , a perfect blend of history and wilderness. Each moment offers the thrill of discovery in a land where time and nature stand still.

This journey unfolds like a desert wind, shifting in texture, tone, and rhythm as it moves across four of India’s most distinctive wilderness habitats. It begins in the lion-ruled forests of Gir, where dry teak woodland and open scrub sustain the last natural population of Asiatic lions, a landscape shaped as much by conservation success as by ancient ecological balance.
Every rustle in the undergrowth carries a sense of quiet authority.

From here, the scenery opens into the luminous grasslands of Velavadar, one of India’s finest and least-altered savannah ecosystems. Vast horizons, seasonal grasses, and salt flats support elegant blackbuck, coursing predators, and a remarkable density of birdlife, offering a visual clarity rare in the subcontinent.

The journey then enters the stark brilliance of the Rann of Kutch, an immense salt desert that feels almost lunar in scale. Here, life has adapted to extremes,Asiatic wild ass move across the white expanse, migratory birds gather at seasonal wetlands, and the silence itself becomes part of the experience. Jawai follows, adding a powerful sense of harmony between people, stone, and wildlife.
Ancient granite hills shelter leopards that coexist with pastoral communities, temples rising naturally from rock formations shaped over millennia.

The expedition concludes in the sweeping isolation of the Desert National Park, where arid grasslands and sand dunes support some of India’s most specialised desert species. Together, these regions form a rare and revealing portrait of India’s western wildlands,diverse, resilient, and deeply evocative.

body: Arrive in India’s capital and explore the contrasts of Old and New Delhi. Wander through bustling bazaars, historic mosques, or iconic landmarks such as India Gate and Humayun’s Tomb before settling into your hotel.
Travel to Agra to experience the magnificence of the Taj Mahal. Visit the Agra Fort and enjoy the changing hues of the marble masterpiece as the day transitions from afternoon to evening.

Continue to Ranthambhore National Park for two days of wildlife exploration. Embark on guided safaris in search of Bengal Tigers, Sloth Bears, and rich birdlife amid ancient ruins, serene lakes, and the dramatic cliffs surrounding the Ranthambhore Fort.

Journey to Jaipur, the Pink City known for its vibrant markets and regal heritage. Discover the Amber Fort, City Palace, and Hawa Mahal, and enjoy free time to shop for textiles, jewellery, and handicrafts. Relax in a heritage palace or luxury boutique retreat.
After a leisurely morning in Jaipur, transfer to the airport for your onward journey. Optional extensions include Delhi, Udaipur, Varanasi, or other destinations across Rajasthan.

The Golden Triangle with Tigers tour seamlessly weaves together India’s cultural heartland and its most iconic wildlife landscapes. Delhi’s dynamic streets set the rhythm of the nation, Agra’s marble mausoleum reveals a timeless love story carved in stone, and Ranthambore National Park introduces the quiet thrill of tracking tigers through forests once shaped by royal hunts.
The journey culminates in Jaipur, where palaces, hilltop forts, and bustling bazaars bring the experience to a vibrant crescendo.

Together, these moments offer an authentic and immersive portrait of India, its artistry, heritage, and natural beauty crafted to inspire, enrich, and captivate first-time and seasoned travellers alike.

India holds many paradises within one. This journey moves fluidly across the country’s diverse wilderness, from the lush, river-fed floodplains of the Northeast to the ancient forests and arid plains of the West, uniting India’s most iconic wildlife in a single, sweeping expedition.

Explore a UNESCO World Heritage Site, seek out India’s Big 5, and encounter rare marvels such as the Golden Tiger, while retreating each evening to handpicked lodges and refined luxury stays.

Fully inclusive and thoughtfully customisable, the experience blends powerful wildlife encounters with seamless travel, cultural depth, and the option of flying in effortless comfort aboard our company-owned business jets.

Travel through four distinct wilderness regions as you follow the trails of India’s Big 5 across iconic national parks, including a UNESCO World Heritage Site shaped by centuries of natural rhythm. Rare species such as the Golden Tiger lend the journey its quiet magic, while an extraordinary diversity of birdlife,over 400 species,animates each landscape.

Fully curated and all-inclusive, with the option of private jet travel and cultural extensions, the experience is defined by unhurried exploration, discretion, and refined ease.

body: Arrive in India’s dynamic capital, where Mughal grandeur meets modern energy. Settle into your hotel, prepare for the adventure ahead, or explore Delhi’s rich heritage, bustling markets, and culinary delights at your own pace.

The journey shifts into the emerald world of Assam as you travel to Kaziranga, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famed for its thriving population of One-horned Rhinos. Dawn and dusk safaris reveal vast floodplains alive with Elephants, Water Buffalo, deer, and an astonishing array of birdlife.

At times, the tall elephant grass parts to reveal something even rarer , the Golden Tiger, a mesmerizing color morph that has made headlines in recent years. The Brahmaputra River frames this wilderness, adding depth and drama to every scene.

Ranthambhore blends natural beauty with the echoes of Rajasthan’s royal past. Each safari takes you through lakes, crumbling temples, and the shadow of the thousand-year-old fort while offering world-class opportunities to photograph Bengal Tigers. Leopards, Sloth Bears, Jackals, and a diversity of bird species add richness to the landscape.
Your stay balances thrilling wildlife encounters with the region’s warm hospitality and luxurious comfort.

The final chapter unfolds in the western dry forests of Gir,the only place on Earth where Asiatic Lions still roam free. Their presence is powerful and unmistakable, transforming each safari into an intimate glimpse into the life of a species saved from the brink. Alongside lions, Gir offers sightings of Leopards, Hyenas, and diverse herbivores moving through teak and acacia woodlands.
This concluding segment ties together India’s Big 5 in a way no other journey can.

This expedition unfolds across India’s most significant wildlife landscapes, each chosen for its ecological importance and iconic species. It begins in Assam’s fertile floodplains, where river-fed grasslands sustain thriving populations of one-horned rhinos, elephants, and abundant birdlife.
The journey then moves to Ranthambhore, where ancient forts overlook forests and lakes that support one of India’s finest tiger habitats, offering rare insight into big-cat behaviour.

The journey concludes in Gir, the last natural refuge of the Asiatic Lion,a conservation success shaped by focused protection and coexistence. Together, these regions form a seamless narrative of grassland, forest, and dry woodland ecosystems, offering the rare privilege of experiencing India’s Big 5 across their native realms in a single, carefully curated journey.

journeys.title: India’s Small Cats Safari
journeys.description: Felines have held human imagination since antiquity, woven into myth and memory..
journeys.intro:
Felines have held human imagination since antiquity, woven into myth and memory. While the great cats command reverence, their smaller kin remain shadows, reclusive, secretive, and exquisitely adapted to life unseen. Every encounter with them feels earned, fleeting, and profoundly intimate.

This expedition is conceived as a quiet pursuit of those rarities: India’s elusive small cats, the true phantoms of the wild. Spanning 21 days, the journey traces an elegant arc across India’s most contrasting ecosystems, each selected for its potential to reveal a different small cat species.

From the mangrove-fringed wetlands near Kolkata to the vast grasslands of Velavadar, the sculpted granite hills of Jawai, and the stark desert margins around Jaisalmer, the expedition reveals how climate, terrain, and isolation have shaped these remarkable predators.

Night drives and nocturnal explorations, time-intensive tracking with specialist naturalists, and extended stays in each landscape create rare opportunities for observation and photography, without haste or intrusion. This is a deeply immersive, once-in-a-lifetime passage into India’s most enigmatic carnivores and the extraordinary landscapes they quietly inhabit.

body: Spanning 21 days, the journey traces an elegant arc across India’s most contrasting ecosystems, each selected for its potential to reveal a different small cat species.

This 21-day specialist journey traverses four distinct habitats,urban wetlands, open grasslands, rugged rocky hills, and arid desert ecosystems,offering rare opportunities to photograph India’s most elusive small cats, including the fishing cat, jungle cat, rusty-spotted cat, and desert cat.

Designed as a fully inclusive and seamlessly orchestrated wilderness experience, the expedition combines expert-led exploration with exceptional photographic access, while ensuring effortless travel aboard company-owned business jets. Guests may also choose to extend the journey to India’s iconic tiger reserves, creating one of the most comprehensive and immersive wild-India expeditions available.

Arrive in Kolkata and settle into the rhythm of eastern India’s cultural capital. By night, explore the fringes of the city where wetlands, fishponds, and mangrove edges support thriving populations of the elusive Fishing Cat. Expert trackers lead nocturnal excursions offering rare photographic opportunities. Days allow time to experience Kolkata’s vibrant markets, colonial heritage, and culinary landscape.

Travel west to Velavadar, a vast expanse of golden grasslands home to Jungle Cats, Indian Wolves, Jackals, and Blackbuck herds. Early mornings and late afternoons provide optimal light as Jungle Cats hunt rodents and birds across open plains. With extended time in the ecosystem, you can focus on behavior, tracking, and long-lens photography while enjoying the serene, open landscapes.

Continue to Jawai, where granite boulders, caves, and scrub forest create ideal terrain for the Rusty-spotted Cat , the world’s smallest wild cat. Safaris traverse rocky outcrops also known for thriving Leopard populations and dramatic scenery. Spend unhurried days and nights exploring this unique co-existence landscape, capturing rare species in rugged, atmospheric settings.

Enter the stark beauty of the Thar Desert, where sweeping dunes and sparse scrub support the adaptable Desert Cat. With its superb camouflage, sightings reward patient scanning and quiet observation. Track natural water sources and rodent hotspots, while also photographing desert foxes, eagles, vultures, and other arid-zone specialists. Evenings highlight some of India’s finest desert skies.

Conclude your journey with a transfer to Jaisalmer Airport. Optional extensions include Ranthambhore for Tigers, Gir for Asiatic Lions, or Ladakh for Snow Leopards , allowing you to build the most comprehensive cat-focused expedition in India.

The journey unfolds as a rare passage through India’s most diverse small-cat landscapes, each region offering a distinct setting and signature encounter. The wetlands around Kolkata introduce the fishing cat, a globally vulnerable species and one of the few felines in the world adapted to semi-aquatic life, often encountered along marshes and canals at dusk.

In the open grasslands of Velavadar, jungle cats move with confidence through tall grasses and scrub, drawn by abundant prey and the wide-open visibility of one of India’s finest remaining grassland ecosystems.

Jawai’s ancient granite hills bring a sense of intimacy and rarity, offering one of the best chances to encounter the rusty-spotted cat, the smallest wild cat on Earth, seldom seen despite its presence across parts of India.

The journey concludes in the Thar Desert, where patience is rewarded as the desert cat, among the country’s least-observed felines, emerges briefly against moonlit dunes, shaped by extremes of heat, wind, and scarcity. Together, these landscapes create a seamless narrative of discovery, a richly layered exploration of India’s most elusive wild cats and the extraordinary terrains they inhabit.

journeys.title: Ladakh - Land of high passes
journeys.description: This voyage unfurls like a meditation across a land that feels both primal and deeply contemplative.
journeys.intro:
This voyage unfurls like a meditation across a land that feels both primal and deeply contemplative. In Ladakh, colour arrives sparingly yet with intent. Turquoise lakes set against vast sweeps of ochre rock, whitewashed monasteries clinging improbably to cliffs, and prayer flags fluttering amidst profound stillness.

The landscape asks for presence, revealing itself slowly through shifting light, deep silence, and scale. Within this rarefied milieu, the journey opens a window to some of the Himalaya’s most extraordinary life forms.

The expedition seamlessly weaves cultural discovery with rare wildlife encounters, offering the exceptional opportunity to observe snow leopards and the elusive Pallas’ cat in their remote, high-altitude domain.

From the vibrant bazaars and Tibetan rhythms of Leh to the sweeping silence of the trans-Himalayan plateau, each moment unfolds amid dramatic scenery, resilient alpine fauna, and a quiet spiritual gravity. Seamless travel, thoughtfully chosen stays, and some of the best trackers from the region make the experience truly rewarding.

This tour is a powerful synthesis of serenity, adventure, and elemental beauty.

Guided by expert trackers and long-standing local partnerships essential for operating in this demanding terrain, the journey offers rare chances to observe snow leopards and the elusive Pallas’ cat, alongside hardy alpine species such as blue sheep and ibex. Thoughtfully paced and seamlessly supported, the experience balances rugged exploration with carefully chosen comforts , from warm, intimate lodges to effortless transfers aboard our business jets. Designed with precision and respect for place, this expedition reflects Safari Crafters’ commitment to exceptional field expertise, trusted collaborations, and a level of care that allows guests to experience Ladakh’s extremes with confidence, depth, and quiet refinement.

Arrive in India’s bustling capital and settle into your hotel. Rest and prepare for your flight into the high Himalayas the following morning.

Fly to Leh with breathtaking aerial views of the snow-bound peaks. Spend two days acclimatizing while exploring Leh’s monasteries, markets, and Tibetan-influenced culture. Gentle walks and guided visits prepare you for higher altitudes ahead.

Enter the vast wilderness of Hemis National Park, home to one of the world’s highest densities of Snow Leopards. With expert trackers, follow the trails of the “Grey Ghost” across ridges and valleys. Each day offers opportunities to photograph mountain wildlife including Himalayan Blue Sheep, Ibex, Red Foxes, and numerous high-altitude birds.
Nights are spent in warm, comfortable lodges or homestays tuned to the extreme climate.

Travel to Pangong Lake (summer only) to witness its shifting turquoise hues set against stark mountains. Continue to Hanle, an isolated plateau renowned for sightings of the rare Pallas’ Cat and high-altitude species such as the Black-necked Crane. The region’s silence, night skies, and sweeping vistas offer unmatched Himalayan solitude.
Return to Leh for your scenic flight back to Delhi, carrying memories of stark deserts, sacred monasteries, and the elusive cats of the high Himalayas.

Ladakh is one of the planet’s most extreme inhabited landscapes, a high-altitude desert where survival is shaped by altitude, weather, and time itself. The journey begins in Leh, where gradual acclimatisation is essential, and where centuries-old Tibetan-Buddhist culture offers insight into how human life has adapted to thin air, long winters, and vast isolation.

From Leh, the expedition moves into the immense expanse of Hemis National Park, the largest protected area in India and one of the most important snow leopard landscapes in the world. This rugged terrain of razor-edged ridges, deep valleys, and scree slopes supports a finely balanced alpine ecosystem, with blue sheep and Ibex forming the prey base that sustains the snow leopard.
Wildlife encounters here are earned through patience, skilled tracking, and an intimate understanding of terrain and movement.

The journey then opens into the vast trans-Himalayan plateaus of Pangong Lake and Hanle, where altitude increases and the landscape broadens into sweeping valleys and high-altitude wetlands. These regions support specialised species such as the Pallas’ cat and migratory cranes, while remote monasteries and nomadic settlements reflect centuries of spiritual resilience.
Together, these landscapes reveal Ladakh in its fullest form, stark, demanding, and profoundly alive, offering a rare understanding of one of the world’s most formidable wilderness regions.

journeys.title: Palaces and Tigers
journeys.description: This is royalty, undistilled and uncompromising.
journeys.intro:
This is royalty, undistilled and uncompromising. A journey that moves through time itself, where every stone carries memory and every horizon bears witness to human endurance and imagination. Across Rajasthan’s royal heartlands, power is etched into the land: desert strongholds, lake-bound palaces, and cities shaped by centuries of ambition and artistry.

Here, history is not observed; it surrounds you. In the forests of Ranthambhore, royalty takes on an older meaning. Amid ruined citadels, banyan trees, and still lakes, the tiger appears, not as spectacle, but as presence. A single, electric moment where breath pauses and time narrows.

The encounter is fleeting, unscripted, and deeply humbling, imprinting itself as a core memory for a lifetime. This is where human legacy meets the wild sovereign of the forest,distinct, powerful, and unforgettable.
highlights: Move through Rajasthan’s royal heartlands on a journey shaped by shifting landscapes and lived-in history. Desert forts rise from the sands, palace facades shimmer on still lakes, and bazaars hum with colour, craft, and ritual. Along the way, the wild reveals itself in many forms,through early-morning forest tracks, granite hills warmed by the sun, distant alarm calls, and skies alive with birdlife. Moments of quiet observation are balanced by encounters that quicken the pulse, culminating in the rare privilege of witnessing India’s great cats in their natural realm. Evenings unfold in thoughtfully chosen heritage hotels, wilderness lodges, and palace retreats, where comfort and character are inseparable. Private jet travel and iconic extensions, including the Taj Mahal, allow the journey to flow effortlessly from one chapter to the next.

Arrive in India’s capital and settle into your hotel. Explore the city at leisure or simply unwind before your Rajasthan adventure begins.

Travel to Ranthambhore National Park, where ancient temples and fort walls rise above lakes and forests. Enjoy multiple safaris tracking Tigers, Leopards, Sloth Bears, and abundant birdlife. Evenings at your lodge offer comfort and the chance to discuss the day’s sightings with naturalists.

Head to Jaipur, the Pink City known for its vibrant markets and architectural grandeur. Visit the Amber Fort, City Palace, and Hawa Mahal, or browse lively bazaars filled with textiles, jewelry, and crafts. Jaipur’s mix of artistry, history, and color sets the tone for Rajasthan’s regal heritage.

Begin in Jaisalmer, where golden havelis and the towering desert fort seem to emerge from the sands. Explore its ornately carved mansions, royal chambers, and sweeping dunes glowing at sunset. Continue to Jodhpur, dominated by the majestic Mehrangarh Fort. Wander through its ramparts and the old city’s blue-hued lanes, with optional leopard-viewing

Arrive in the granite-studded landscape of Jawai , a place where wild Leopards live in harmony with local herding communities. Spend your days tracking these elusive cats, exploring rocky outcrops, and enjoying the tranquility of one of India’s most unique wildlife regions.

Conclude your journey in Udaipur, the City of Lakes. Cruise across Lake Pichola, explore the majestic City Palace, and relax in your lakeside retreat surrounded by mountain views. Depart from Udaipur with a deeper connection to Rajasthan’s cultural and natural heritage.

Rajasthan reads like an epic, its cities, forts, and wild landscapes revealing one chapter at a time. The forests of Ranthambhore draw you into a world where ancient ruins are reclaimed by wilderness, and tigers move with quiet authority through terrain once shaped by kings and conquest.

Jaipur follows in vivid contrast, alive with colour, craftsmanship, and ceremony, its palaces, avenues, and bazaars reflecting centuries of Rajput artistry and courtly life. Deeper into the desert, Jaisalmer rises like a mirage of honeyed stone, followed by Jodhpur’s indigo labyrinth, crowned by a formidable fort overlooking the vast Thar.

Jawai offers an unexpected harmony: leopards moving freely among pastoral communities, within a landscape of ancient granite shaped by generations of coexistence. Finally, Udaipur softens the journey’s edges with shimmering lakes, island palaces, and a gentler rhythm shaped by water, light, and reflection.
Together, these moments compose a refined narrative of beauty, resilience, wilderness, and royal legacy, the enduring essence of Rajputana.

journeys.title: Pink City with Pink Panthers
journeys.description: Jaipur is a symphony of heritage and lineage, of grandeur and simple tidings.
journeys.intro:
Jaipur is a symphony of heritage and lineage, of grandeur and simple tidings. Palaces rise with quiet confidence, their latticed windows filtering light the way memory filters time, while mighty forts crown distant hills, standing sentinel over centuries of ambition, artistry, and royal command. Yet Jaipur is also untamed.

Just beyond the city’s vibrant pulse lies Jhalana Leopard Reserve, a rare and unexpected wilderness where leopards move silently through rocky ridges and scrub forests, and jungle cats slip between shadows at dusk.

Jaipur stands as one of India’s earliest planned royal cities, shaped by principles of Vedic architecture and astronomy. Its forts, palaces, and harmonious street layouts reflect the vision, power, and artistic legacy of the Rajput rulers. Beyond this historic urban fabric lies Jhalana, once a royal hunting landscape and today a protected forest at the city’s edge.
Here, leopards and other native wildlife move through rocky hills and dry deciduous woodland, revealing a rare and compelling coexistence of wilderness and urban life.

journeys.title: Royal Rajasthan Safari
journeys.description: Rajasthan unfolds as a land of layered histories, dramatic landscapes, and enduring regal traditions.
journeys.intro:
Rajasthan unfolds as a land of layered histories, dramatic landscapes, and enduring regal traditions. From arid plains and ancient forests to granite hills and walled cities, this region hosts a remarkable mosaic of habitats shaped by centuries of rule, culture, and resilience.

This immersive journey traces a refined arc through India’s most storied heartland,beginning with the architectural grandeur of Delhi and Agra, before venturing into the tiger-haunted ruins of Ranthambhore.

The experience then unfolds through the royal elegance of Jaipur and Udaipur, moves into leopard country amid Jawai’s striking granite formations, and concludes in the timeless splendour of Jodhpur, the Blue City of the Rajputs.
highlights: Discover Rajasthan’s royal and untamed spirit as you travel through historic cities, ancient forts, and vibrant wilderness landscapes. Enjoy expertly guided safaris in Ranthambhore and Jawai, stay in exquisite heritage hotels, and savour the region’s legendary cuisine. This journey seamlessly weaves together culture, wildlife, and refined luxury across some of India’s most iconic destinations.

Enjoy expertly guided safaris in Ranthambhore and Jawai, stay in exquisite heritage hotels, and savour the region’s legendary cuisine. This journey seamlessly weaves together culture, wildlife, and refined luxury across some of India’s most iconic destinations.

Arrive in India’s capital and explore its striking contrasts of Mughal monuments, colonial avenues, and vibrant marketplaces. Travel to Agra to witness the Taj Mahal in the golden light of dawn or dusk and visit the impressive Agra Fort. Evenings are spent in comfort at one of the region’s finest hotels.

Travel to Ranthambhore National Park, famed for its tigers roaming freely amidst ancient temples and crumbling Rajput fortifications. Enjoy guided safaris across lakes, grasslands, and rocky hillscapes. Between drives, relax at your lodge while immersing yourself in the rhythms of the forest.

Fly to Jaipur, the Pink City, where the Amber Fort, City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and artisanal bazaars showcase Rajasthan’s royal artistry. Continue to Udaipur, the romantic city of lakes, where the shimmering Lake Pichola reflects palaces, temples, and ghats. Enjoy boat rides, heritage walks, and serene luxury.

Enter the dramatic landscapes of Jawai, where huge granite boulders conceal thriving leopard populations living alongside Rabari shepherds. Embark on leopard safaris, visit pastoral settlements, and experience the tranquillity of the Jawai Dam,often a haven for flamingos and migratory birds.

Conclude your journey in Jodhpur, the Blue City. Explore the majestic Mehrangarh Fort rising above a sea of indigo homes, marvel at the stepwells, stroll through the vibrant Sardar Market, and savor the city’s rich Marwari cuisine. Depart from Jodhpur with memories of Rajasthan’s royal soul.

Your Royal Rajasthan Safari opens in Delhi, a city forged by ambition and empire. From the rise and fall of Sultanates and Mughal dynasties to the quiet order of the British Raj, power has shaped this capital in stone and memory. Its monuments stand like chronicles of conquest and vision.
From here, you travel to Agra to stand before the Taj Mahal, born of love and loss, and walk the ramparts of Agra Fort, where emperors once ruled and destiny was decided.

The journey then turns toward Ranthambhore, where a 10th-century fort looms above forests, lakes, and abandoned temples. Once a royal hunting ground, this land has reclaimed its wild soul. Tigers move through ruins and shadows, and history yields to the primal rhythm of the forest.

From wilderness to royalty, you arrive in Jaipur, the meticulously planned capital of the Kachwaha Rajputs. Pink-hued streets, grand palaces, and celestial observatories reflect a civilisation guided by order, science, and artistry. Udaipur follows,romantic and resolute. Here, white palaces rise from still waters, carrying the legacy of the Mewar rulers who chose resistance over surrender.

journeys.title: Southern Splendour
journeys.description: This sojourn leads into a verdant world of exceptional richness, where South India’s forests and highland ecosystems form one of the subcontinent’s most vital wildlife.
journeys.intro:
This sojourn leads into a verdant world of exceptional richness, where South India’s forests and highland ecosystems form one of the subcontinent’s most vital wildlife corridors. A globally recognised biodiversity hotspot, the landscape unfolds in layers of rolling cloud, blue-tinged hills, emerald meadows, and rivers that murmur as they thread through ancient forests.

The journey traces a graceful natural arc, from the tranquil backwaters of Kabini to the storied tiger country of Bandipur, where the rare privilege exists to encounter tigers, leopards, herds of elephants, wild dogs, and sloth bears within a single landscape. Few places in India offer such a remarkable concentration of wildlife in such compelling settings.
highlights: This immersive journey explores two of South India’s premier wildlife regions, where a combination of boat and land safaris reveals large congregations of elephants and offers excellent opportunities to observe tigers, leopards, and the endangered wild dog. Travelling through the biodiverse Western Ghats, you may encounter rare primates, reptiles, and amphibians, along with iconic species such as the lion-tailed macaque and the Nilgiri tahr, and a remarkable range of endemic wildlife found nowhere else on Earth. With forests accessible year-round and expert naturalists guiding each exploration, this all-inclusive itinerary delivers uninterrupted and deeply enriching wildlife experiences.

Each region reveals its own distinct signatures, elephant herds gathering along forested waterways, wild dogs coursing through dry forests, the elusive lion-tailed macaque inhabiting deep valleys, and Nilgiri tahr poised on wind-swept cliffs.
With varied habitats, expert naturalists, and seamless logistics, the itinerary distils the ecological depth and layered biodiversity that define South India’s wilderness.

Drive to Kabini, a lush landscape shaped by backwaters, riverine forests, and open fields. This region is renowned for its large Elephant congregations and excellent opportunities to observe Leopards, Tigers, and Wild Dogs. Alternate between boat and jeep safaris for varied photographic angles and a deeper understanding of animal movement around water systems.
Evenings at camp offer guided discussions on behavior, tracking, and Kabini’s ecological significance.

Continue into Bandipur National Park, a key component of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Bandipur’s dry deciduous forests, rolling hills, and scenic streams support Tigers, Leopards, Elephants, Gaur, and abundant birdlife. Early morning safaris provide the best light for photography, while afternoon drives reveal predators on the move.
Your naturalist helps interpret signs and patterns, creating rewarding, informed wildlife encounters.

Head toward the Anamalais, known for deep valleys, forested slopes, and rich endemism. Track the elusive Lion-tailed Macaque while exploring evergreen forests alive with reptiles, amphibians, and birds found nowhere else. The region’s unique ecology reveals how altitude and terrain shape species diversity across the Western Ghats.

Travel to Eravikulam National Park, home to high-altitude grasslands and the endemic Nilgiri Tahr. Hike along designated trails offering sweeping views of mist-covered mountains, shola forests, and tea estates. Sightings of montane birds, rare frogs, and specialized flora highlight this biodiversity hotspot. Depart from Kochi after a vivid journey spanning South India’s most iconic wilderness landscapes.

The route through Kabini, Bandipur, and the Western Ghats unfolds South India’s wilderness as a seamless ecological progression. Kabini sets the tone with its river-driven habitats, where seasonal waters draw large elephant congregations and predators quietly patrol the forested edges. Bandipur alters the cadence to drier deciduous forests and open grasslands, creating expansive sightlines and vivid predator-prey interactions.

As the journey enters the Ghats, the landscape rises and deepens, steep valleys and ancient rainforests sheltering isolated evolutionary lineages of primates, amphibians, and birds found nowhere else. The experience culminates in Eravikulam, where high-altitude grasslands and rugged escarpments form the stronghold of the Nilgiri tahr, poised against cliffs beneath drifting cloud.
Together, these landscapes reveal a region defined by layered diversity, ecological continuity, and quietly extraordinary wildlife encounters.

journeys.title: Terrific Terai
journeys.description: The Shivalik Range and the Terai together form a living threshold between mountain and plain, where the Himalaya slowly loosens into forested foothills, braided rivers,.
journeys.intro:
The Shivalik Range and the Terai together form a living threshold between mountain and plain, where the Himalaya slowly loosens into forested foothills, braided rivers, and fertile grasslands. Shaped by monsoon rhythms and ancient geology, this breathing landscape sustains an extraordinary richness of life.

The journey follows this wild corridor across four distinct reserves, each with its own character and pulse, from Corbett’s riverine forests, where tigers and elephants move through mist and water, to Rajaji’s sal woodlands resonant with birdsong and elusive leopards; from the quiet, little-trodden wilderness of Pilibhit to the wetland-laced expanses of Dudhwa.

Together, these landscapes unfold as a poetic passage of adventure and patience, offering intimate encounters with nature in all its shifting moods. Explore four iconic sanctuaries across the Terai and Shivalik foothills, each offering exceptional wildlife encounters with tigers, leopards, elephants, swamp deer, and rich birdlife.

Journey through a mosaic of forests, wetlands, and river systems, accessing lesser-visited wilderness areas that allow for more intimate and rewarding sightings. Accompanied by expert naturalists, and with the option of seamless travel via company-owned business jets, this all-inclusive itinerary delivers a deeply immersive and refined wildlife experience.

Arrive in India’s capital and settle in before your journey into the Terai begins. Your naturalist will conduct a brief orientation outlining upcoming landscapes, species, and logistics.

Travel to Jim Corbett National Park, India’s oldest tiger reserve. Its mix of riverine belts, dense sal forests, and wide grasslands offers ideal habitats for Bengal Tigers, Leopards, and Elephants. Morning and afternoon jeep safaris take you through varying terrain, increasing chances of sightings.
Corbett’s rivers support rich birdlife and crocodilians, while quiet forest trails reveal signs of movement from Jackals, Deer, and other mammals.

Continue to Rajaji National Park, where the foothills of the Himalayas meet sweeping grasslands. The park’s mosaic of riverine and sal forests supports Tigers, Leopards, and India’s largest Elephants herds. Open areas provide excellent photographic opportunities of ungulates such as Swamp Deer and Wild Boar. Birders enjoy sightings of hornbills, woodpeckers, and raptors patrolling the valleys.

Move into the quieter, less-visited wilderness of Philibit. Its forests and fields hold Leopards, Jungle Cats, Hyenas, and rich bird diversity. Safaris here focus on tracking signs, observing behavior, and exploring landscapes shaped by human-wildlife coexistence. The gentle pace allows for immersive nature photography and meaningful time in the field.

End your journey in the biodiverse expanses of Dudhwa National Park. Explore tall grasslands, wetlands, and dense sal forests on boat and jeep safaris. Look for endangered Swamp Deer, Marsh Crocodiles, and birdlife that thrives around its river systems. Trails occasionally reveal signs of Tigers and Leopards moving through the undergrowth. Evenings are reserved for debriefings, stargazing, or relaxed time in the lodge.

The journey through the Terai and Shivaliks unfolds as a gradual passage through some of India’s most dynamic ecosystems. Jim Corbett National Park sets the tone with dramatic river valleys and evocative dawn choruses, where tigers move silently through sal forests and elephants appear along riverbanks without warning.
In Rajaji National Park, the landscape opens into grasslands and wooded slopes, with the possibility of encountering leopards in their feral Shivalik habitat amid bird-rich sal forests.

The experience deepens at Pilibhit Tiger Reserve, where tall grasslands and quiet forest corridors offer a genuine chance of spotting a tiger moving through dense vegetation, an intimate and memorable sight unique to this landscape. The journey concludes at Dudhwa National Park, where wetlands and towering grasses reflect a world shaped by monsoon rhythms and seasonal migrations.
Together, these reserves reveal the larger story of the Terai: a vital wildlife corridor experienced with depth, comfort, and unhurried immersion.

From these cool, mist-draped heights, the journey descends into the lush, life-filled floodplains of Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its stronghold of Indian journey continues with a special visit to the Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary, where India’s only apes, the agile Hoolock Gibbon, move through the canopy, their calls echoing through ancient forest.

Guided by expert naturalists, supported by seamless logistics, and directly contributing to Red Panda conservation, this meticulously curated expedition unites Himalayan grandeur, iconic wildlife, and immersive natural beauty into a journey that lingers long after it ends.

body: This immersive 12-day expedition brings together two of India’s most compelling ecosystems,the high-altitude forests of Singalila and the UNESCO-protected floodplains of Kaziranga,into one fluid journey. Discover rare and iconic species including the Red Panda, Indian one-horned rhino, Hoolock gibbon, and exceptional Himalayan birdlife, framed by rhododendron blooms and vast mountain vistas.
Led by expert naturalists and supported by seamless travel arrangements, the journey combines elevated comfort with direct contributions to Red Panda conservation.
Arrive in India’s vibrant capital and settle in before your journey into the Eastern Himalayas. Depending on your arrival time, you may explore Delhi’s bustling markets or relax at your hotel.
Fly to Bagdogra and overnight in Siliguri, the gateway to the Himalayan foothills. Prepare for your ascent to the high-altitude forests of Singalila the next morning.

Travel up to the Singalila Ridge, famed for breathtaking views of the world’s highest peaks and for being the best place on earth to see the elusive Red Panda. Spend your days trekking, scanning forest canopies, watching for colourful Himalayan birds, and exploring rhododendron-lined trails with your expert trackers.

Fly to Guwahati and continue to Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its Indian One-horned Rhino population. Enjoy morning and afternoon jeep safaris through grasslands, wetlands, and woodland patches while seeking elephants, wild buffalo, big cats, and diverse birdlife.
A dedicated day visit to the Gibbon Sanctuary offers close encounters with Hoolock Gibbons , India’s only apes , as they move gracefully through the treetops.
Return to Guwahati for your flight to Delhi, where your journey concludes. You may opt to extend your tour to India’s tiger reserves for an enhanced wildlife experience.

Your journey begins with a gentle ascent from Delhi into the Himalayan foothills, where cooler air and rising ridgelines signal a shift into the temperate forests of Singalila Ridge. Here, oak and rhododendron forests cloak the slopes, forming one of the subcontinent’s most important transboundary habitats and one of the few regions where the elusive Red Panda survives.
Exploration is slow and on foot, guided by expert trackers, offering first-time travellers an authentic understanding of Himalayan wildlife and altitude-driven ecosystems.

The landscape then transforms dramatically as you descend into Assam’s fertile floodplains and enter Kaziranga National Park, home to over 2,600 Indian one-horned rhinos, the largest population anywhere in the world, along with elephants and prolific birdlife sustained by the Brahmaputra’s annual floods.

A visit to the Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary adds a rare dimension, protecting around 150 Hoolock gibbons, India’s only apes, whose calls echo through the forest canopy. Together, these landscapes offer a compact yet deeply informative journey through two of Northeast India’s most vital and contrasting ecosystems.

journeys.title: Uttarakhand Wildlife Circuit
journeys.description: There is a quiet poetry to this expedition, written in colour, contour, and the patient craft of nature across Uttarakhand’s most evocative terrains.
journeys.intro:
There is a quiet poetry to this expedition, written in colour, contour, and the patient craft of nature across Uttarakhand’s most evocative terrains. It reveals itself in sinuous rivers edged with pale stone, the austere grace of towering sal forests, and gentle transitions where grasslands open into wide, breathing valleys.

Light shifts constantly here, filtered through canopy, reflected off water, softened by mist, shaping landscapes that feel ancient yet alive. The journey begins in the storied forests of Jim Corbett National Park, where the Terai plains and Shivalik foothills converge in a mosaic of sal forests, riverine belts, and grasslands.

Tigers, leopards, elephants, and rich birdlife move through terrain long shaped by water and time. From here, the trail flows into the quiet magnificence of Rajaji National Park, a riverine wilderness where elephant herds traverse forest corridors and predators thrive in open, light-filled landscapes.
highlights: Explore Uttarakhand’s varied wilderness, from tiger-rich Terai forests to the serene Himalayan birding enclaves of Chopta, Sattal, and Pangot. Enjoy opportunities to photograph tigers, leopards, elephants, and an extraordinary array of Himalayan birds across contrasting landscapes. Seamlessly curated and all-inclusive, the journey blends jeep safaris, gentle treks, and guided nature walks led by expert naturalists, complemented by optional private jet travel for effortless comfort.

From here, the trail flows into the quiet magnificence of Rajaji National Park, a riverine wilderness where elephant herds traverse forest corridors and predators thrive in open, light-filled landscapes.

The ascent into the Himalaya shifts both mood and altitude, leading to the tranquil forests and ridgelines of Chopta, Sattal, and Pangot. Here, rhododendron and oak forests frame alpine meadows, distant snow peaks, and quiet trails, a sanctuary for birdlife and reflective walks. Together, these landscapes shape a deeply immersive journey through one of India’s most biodiverse and visually stirring regions.

Explore Uttarakhand’s varied wilderness, from tiger-rich Terai forests to the serene Himalayan birding enclaves of Chopta, Sattal, and Pangot. Enjoy opportunities to photograph tigers, leopards, elephants, and an extraordinary array of Himalayan birds across contrasting landscapes.

Seamlessly curated and all-inclusive, the journey blends jeep safaris, gentle treks, and guided nature walks led by expert naturalists, complemented by optional private jet travel for effortless comfort.
Arrive in India’s capital and settle in before your Himalayan adventure. Depending on arrival time, explore Delhi’s cultural highlights or relax at your hotel.

Travel to Corbett, India’s oldest tiger reserve and a landscape of sal forests, meadows, and riverbanks. Enjoy multiple jeep safaris in prime tiger territory, with chances to encounter Leopards, Elephants, Gharials, Otters, and rich birdlife. Mornings bring soft forest light ideal for photography, while evenings offer calm river views and the ambience of the Himalayan foothills.

Continue to Rajaji, spread across the Shivalik foothills. Safari drives explore riverine belts and open forest where Elephants move gracefully and predators such as Tigers and Leopards are often seen. The habitat diversity supports birds, ungulates, and smaller mammals, creating excellent opportunities for wildlife viewing and landscape photography.

Ascend into the Himalayas for a completely different wilderness experience. Mist-laden forests, tranquil lakes, and rhododendron trails surround Chopta, Pangot, and Sattal,renowned for Himalayan bird species such as the Koklass Pheasant, Himalayan Monal, Cheer Pheasant, and countless migratory visitors. Guided treks and nature walks take
you through meadows, evergreen forests, and lakeshores ideal for photography and peaceful immersion.
Descend from the mountains and return to Delhi for your onward journey.

Your Uttarakhand expedition unfolds across a sequence of ecologically distinct landscapes, each adding depth and context to the journey. It begins in Jim Corbett National Park, India’s oldest national park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, a landmark in wildlife conservation.

Located within the Terai belt, Corbett’s sal forests, grasslands, and river systems support one of North India’s most significant tiger populations, alongside elephants, leopards, gharial-rich rivers, and exceptional birdlife shaped by seasonal flooding and fertile alluvial plains.

The journey continues to Rajaji National Park, a vital elephant corridor linking the Terai with the Himalayan foothills. Its open valleys, riverine forests, and Shivalik slopes form a transitional ecosystem where large mammals move freely, offering strong visibility and insight into wildlife movement at the base of the Himalayas.

Ranthambhore sits where the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges meet. Dhok woodland, open meadows, seasonal water and the silhouette of a 10th-century fort give the reserve a visual identity unlike any other major tiger park.

The park is deservedly associated with Bengal tigers, but a considered visit also watches for leopard, sloth bear, sambar, marsh crocodile and raptors. Permit demand is high, so the quality of a journey depends on early booking, sensible zone requests and enough drives to let the forest reveal more than a single sighting.

Jawai is defined by weathered granite, open scrub and villages rather than a fenced reserve. Leopards use caves and ridgelines within a landscape shared with pastoral communities, making local knowledge and respectful field practice central to the experience.

The reservoir adds a second ecological register, drawing crocodiles and seasonal birdlife. A private stay works best at an unhurried pace, with repeated dawn and evening scans rather than any promise of a particular animal appearing on command.

destinations.intro:
Ladakh is sculpted by divine forces. It is where the high Himalaya breathes fierce and free.In this rarefied world of quartz-blue horizons and wind-sculpted ridges, life has learned to endure with remarkable ingenuity. The thin air carries not just silence but song, echoes of migratory cranes over frozen wetlands, the subtle patter of pika in rocky clearings, and the ghost-soft tread of the Snow Leopard across snow-pale slopes. Here, the wilderness thrives too and the landscape gazes back with ancient patience, welcoming one into a wondrous realm of nature.

Ladakh's wildlife lives at the scale of mountains. Hemis National Park and neighbouring valleys support snow leopard, blue sheep, urial, ibex, wolf and high-altitude birds across terrain that demands time and acclimatisation.

Winter offers tracking conditions for specialist snow-leopard journeys; summer opens a wider landscape of wetlands, monasteries and alpine routes. In either season, the itinerary must remain secondary to altitude safety, road conditions and responsible local guidance.

destinations.intro:
Pench Tiger Reserve, spanning the borders of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, is a visually rewarding and deeply evocative wildlife landscape in central India. Bisected by the Pench River, the reserve’s gently undulating terrain creates a varied mosaic of grasslands, wooded slopes, and rocky outcrops, an environment that famously inspired Rudyard Kipling’s The Jungle Book and continues to stir the imagination. Renowned for consistent tiger sightings, Pench is also home to Leopards, Sloth Bears, Dholes, Gaur, and a rich assemblage of deer, supported by a strong and resilient ecosystem. With over 300 bird species, the forest remains animated at every hour.

Pench is a teak-dominated forest of river channels, old village clearings and the wider Totladoh water system. Its fauna includes tiger, leopard, wild dog, gaur and a diverse bird community that changes with season.

The reserve is approached through distinct gates on the Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra sides. A well-built itinerary begins with the permit, then chooses the lodge and transfer, avoiding the common mistake of treating every Pench address as equally close to every safari zone.

Safari operations are regulated and vehicle formats differ. A private plan should set expectations around the available experience, select accommodation for access rather than branding alone, and avoid treating the Mysuru-Ooty road as a substitute for time inside the forest.

destinations.description: The Indian Sundarbans protect a UNESCO-listed tidal mangrove ecosystem where creeks, mudflats and islands support tigers, dolphins, crocodiles and rich birdlife.
destinations.intro:
The Sundarbans are not a conventional tiger safari. They are a tidal world of mangrove islands, estuaries and shifting mudflats, part of the largest mangrove forest on Earth and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Exploration is by boat and governed by tide, weather and forest permission. Tigers are present but difficult to see; the deeper reward is understanding an ecosystem adapted to salt, flood and constant change, including dolphins, crocodiles, reptiles and waterbirds.

destinations.description: Dudhwa is a Terai landscape of sal forest, marsh and tall grass near the Nepal border, supporting tiger, rhino, swamp deer and rare grassland species.
destinations.intro:
At the far northern edge of India, resides a land of dreamy proportion.In the Terai, forests loosen into grass, rivers wander without urgency, and mornings arrive wrapped in mist. Dudhwa Tiger Reserve and Pilibhit Tiger Reserve exist within this gentle geography, offering a tiger landscape that feels unguarded, intimate, and profoundly old. This is where the tiger walks without haste, often straight down endless forest roads, carrying the quiet authority of a land that belongs entirely to it.

Dudhwa protects a surviving reach of the Terai, where sal forest meets tall alluvial grass and wetland. The official tourism board identifies tiger, rhinoceros, swamp deer, elephant, hispid hare and Bengal florican among its conservation significance.

The landscape rewards guests who already understand that wildlife quality is not measured by big-cat frequency alone. Grassland, marsh and forest require different ways of looking, with enough time to appreciate the ecological whole.

A considered starting point, not a fixed package

destinations.homepageCaption: At the meeting edge of plains and hills, Rajaji Tiger Reserve settles into the landscape with quiet ease.
destinations.intro:
At the meeting edge of plains and hills, Rajaji Tiger Reserve settles into the landscape with quiet ease. Less frequented yet deeply important, it lies within one of India’s key ecological corridors, revealing its character gradually rather than all at once. The Terai forest moves gently across sal stands, grasslands, and riverbeds shaped by older flows of water. Pebble-strewn channels wind through the trees; tall grasses sway in the open air; clearings rest beneath wide, unbroken skies. The forest shifts in subtle ways,an elephant herd crossing without urgency, a leopard easing into cover, hornbills passing overhead with steady wingbeats. All around, a living wilderness unfolds at its own pace.

Set across the Shivalik foothills of Uttarakhand, Rajaji Tiger Reserve spans over 820 sq. km of Terai grasslands, riverine forests, and low hill sal woodlands. Formed through the consolidation of Chilla, Motichur, and Rajaji landscapes, it serves as a vital ecological link between the Ganga plains and the Himalayan foothills. While tigers remain a keystone presence, recent years have seen a notable rise in leopard activity, particularly across the Mohand Range and adjoining forest tracts. These cats move confidently through the mosaic terrain, using dry riverbeds as corridors and forest interiors where cover and prey converge. Asian elephants migrate seasonally through the reserve, accompanied by diverse ungulates and over 300 species of birds that animate the canopy and river margins.

destinations.description: Corbett is India's first national park, a river-shaped tiger and elephant landscape across the Himalayan foothills and Terai.
destinations.homepageCaption: Where the foothills of the Himalayas meet the flowing contours of the plains, Corbett Tiger Reserve unfolds as a landscape that feels elemental and quietly meditative.
destinations.intro:
Where the foothills of the Himalayas meet the flowing contours of the plains, Corbett Tiger Reserve unfolds as a landscape that feels elemental and quietly meditative. Shaped by water, wind, and the unhurried passage of time, rivers braid through open grasslands and dense sal forests, carrying the forest’s pulse in every glint of light and sound. The terrain feels expansive yet intimate,bold in scale, but gentle in the way it draws you in. Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, Asia’s first national park, Corbett stands at the very foundation of wildlife conservation in the subcontinent. It was later renamed in honour of Jim Corbett, the legendary hunter-turned-conservationist whose deep respect for these forests helped shape India’s early conservation ethic. In 1973, Corbett became one of the first reserves under Project Tiger, anchoring a national movement that would redefine the future of wildlife protection in India.

Spanning over 1,300 sq. km of core and buffer landscapes, Corbett is a richly layered mosaic of grasslands, riverine belts, marshy hollows, and forested ridges. Anchored by the Ramganga River and framed by the Shivalik foothills, the reserve changes character with every season,mist-laden winter mornings, monsoon greens alive with growth, and dry months when trails and tracks tell their own stories. Tigers move through this landscape with quiet authority, elephants follow age-old paths to water, and birdlife fills the canopy with motion and song. With more than 600 recorded bird species and a remarkable range of mammals, including leopards, sloth bears, Himalayan black bears, deer, and otters, Corbett’s beauty lies in abundance and balance. Here, the familiar and the rare share the same stage, and encounters often arrive without warning.

destinations.homepageCaption: Velavadar is a medley of horizons,a rare testament to openness in a world where grasslands are fast disappearing.
destinations.intro:
Velavadar is a medley of horizons,a rare testament to openness in a world where grasslands are fast disappearing. In the heart of Saurashtra, this quiet jewel stands as a beacon of hope, safeguarding one of the planet’s most threatened ecosystems. Here, the sun caresses the land without bias, and the wilderness reveals itself without concealment. Beauty is expressed freely across flat plains, dry grasses, thorny scrub, and skies that stretch beyond measure. In this landscape, life moves in the open, defined by running blackbucks, hunting wolves, and skies alive with birds that make Velavadar one of India’s great grassland sanctuaries.

Velavadar protects one of India’s last and finest savannah-like grassland ecosystems. Shaped by seasons and proximity to the Gulf of Khambhat, parts of the park transform during the monsoon, when low-lying southern stretches flood to form seasonal wetlands and mudflats. This shifting landscape creates a mosaic of habitats, grasslands, saline flats, scrub, and wetlands, each supporting a distinct cast of life. The park is best known as a stronghold of the blackbuck, with one of the largest and healthiest populations in the country. Alongside them a discreet community of smaller mammals. Here, predators take centre stage: the Indian wolf patrols the plains with quiet authority, while striped hyenas, foxes, golden jackals, and jungle cats follow the rhythms of the open land.Above it all, Velavadar is a birding revelation, home to over a hundred recorded species and one of the world’s most significant winter roosts for migratory harriers, alongside floricans, cranes, flamingos, pelicans, storks, larks, and sandgrouse.

destinations.homepageCaption: Nestled in the lower reaches of the Kumaon Himalayas, Sattal and Pangot stand as a renowned haven for a rich and abundant birdlife.
destinations.intro:
Nestled in the lower reaches of the Kumaon Himalayas, Sattal and Pangot stand as a renowned haven for a rich and abundant birdlife. These two intimate landscapes, teeming with avian spectacle, together form one of India’s most rewarding nature destinations. Here, the measure of wilderness is found in the constant birdsong, the clear reflections on the water, and the quiet unfolding of life among the oak and pine forests.

Sattal,literally meaning seven lakes, is a rare freshwater ecosystem, an interconnected cluster of pristine lakes set amid dense oak and pine forests. Once part of a colonial-era tea-growing belt in Kumaon, the plantations have long receded, leaving behind an unspoiled biome that has drawn naturalists and birdwatchers for decades. The lakes anchor the landscape, creating calm, layered habitats where water, forest, and sky intersect seamlessly. A short climb higher brings you to Pangot, a small mountain village perched at around 6,500 feet. Surrounded by mixed temperate forests of oak, pine, and rhododendron, Pangot has quietly evolved into one of the finest birding locations in the Himalayas too. Its elevation and forest diversity allow species from the plains, mid-hills, and higher altitudes to overlap, making it ecologically rich despite its modest size.

destinations.homepageCaption: In the eastern reaches of Rajasthan, a place of remarkable serenity and ecological harmony, lies Keoladeo National Park.
destinations.intro:
In the eastern reaches of Rajasthan, a place of remarkable serenity and ecological harmony, lies Keoladeo National Park. Universally known as Bharatpur, this park is celebrated as one of the world's most vital avian landscapes. Here, water, grass, and sky converge in delicate equilibrium to create a peaceful haven. Bharatpur is a chorus of symphonic avian wonders, where the very rhythm of life, shaped by migration, nesting, and breeding, is dictated by the arrival of the seasons on wings. It is, truly, a love letter to peace.

Keoladeo’s origins are as remarkable as its present. Created in the 18th century by the Maharajas of Bharatpur through the damming of local rivers, the wetland was initially designed for flood control and royal hunting. Over time, careful protection transformed it from a duck-shooting reserve into a sanctuary, later earning national park status and, in 1985, recognition as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Today, Keoladeo stands as a global benchmark for wetland conservation. Its shallow marshes, seasonally flooded grasslands, mudflats, and wooded patches support an extraordinary diversity of birds,both resident and migratory. More than 370 species have been recorded here, making it one of Asia’s most important heronries and wintering grounds for waterfowl arriving from Central Asia, Siberia, Europe, and beyond.

destinations.intro:
On the very edges of Jaipur, Jhalana exists as a startling contradiction. This is wilderness stitched into the city, an unfenced forest where leopards move freely against the silhouettes of hills, fort walls, and distant urban sprawl. Few places in the world offer such proximity to a large carnivore within a living metropolis, and fewer still do so with such consistency.

Once a reserved hunting forest of Jaipur’s former rulers, Jhalana endured decades of pressure from mining and urban expansion before conservation efforts reversed its decline. Spread across a compact stretch of the ancient Aravalli hills, one of the oldest mountain systems on Earth, Jhalana has emerged as a global example of urban wildlife resilience. Its semi-arid, dry deciduous thorn forest supports one of the highest leopard densities in India, sustained by a strong prey base and minimal disturbance. More than a refuge, Jhalana demonstrates how large predators can persist alongside human settlements when space is respected and thoughtfully managed.

destinations.homepageCaption: Vast, elemental, and almost surreal, the Rann of Kutch is one of the Indian subcontinent’s most extraordinary landscapes.
destinations.intro:
Vast, elemental, and almost surreal, the Rann of Kutch is one of the Indian subcontinent’s most extraordinary landscapes. Here, land and sky stretch into one another, and scale becomes the defining experience. The Rann is not a place of excess life, but of precise adaptation. In winter t wears the

The word Rann refers to a marsh or desert, an apt description for a landscape that shifts dramatically with the seasons. Once part of the Arabian Sea, tectonic movements and river sedimentation transformed this region into a vast seasonal salt desert. Today, it is divided into two distinct yet interconnected regions: the Great Rann of Kutch, a seemingly endless white expanse that floods during the monsoon and crystallises in winter; and the Little Rann of Kutch, a saline desert punctuated by scrub, grasslands, wetlands, and elevated islands known as bets. Ecologically, the Little Rann holds exceptional significance as home to the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary, the last refuge of the endangered Indian wild ass. The Rann also supports vast congregations of migratory birds, most notably flamingos, which breed here in globally significant numbers. Sparse vegetation, salt-tolerant grasses, and specialised desert scrub complete an ecosystem defined by resilience.

expeditions.intro:
Track and photograph the legendary Black Leopard of Laikipia, Kenya, on an exceptionally rare photo safari set within private wilderness landscapes.

This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, among the rarest wildlife encounters on Earth, to witness and document a bold Black Leopard against dramatic savannahs and river valleys, capturing close-up portraits, powerful hunts, and intimate natural behaviour rarely seen anywhere in the world.

Along the way, encounter elephants, wild dogs, and elusive striped hyenas, all framed by Laikipia’s striking light and open terrain. Led by expert guides, this all-inclusive photo expedition offers day and night safaris, placing you at the heart of one of the most coveted and cherished wildlife photography journeys globally.

If you seek an off-beat African safari far removed from the crowds, join us in Northern Kenya for an all-inclusive photographic journey through the wild heart of Laikipia. This rugged plateau, where rolling savannahs dissolve into rocky escarpments and riverine forests, hosts a remarkable diversity of wildlife.

Elephants, Grevy’s zebras, and antelopes move through the open plains, while elusive predators such as leopards, wild dogs, and striped hyenas lend the landscape its raw, untamed edge.

body: Led by expert guides, this all-inclusive photo expedition offers day and night safaris, placing you at the heart of one of the most coveted and cherished wildlife photography journeys globally.

The region’s true icon is the Melanistic Leopard, a rare black variant that has become emblematic of the Laikipia wilderness. Its regular presence and relaxed behaviour around vehicles make it one of the most coveted photographic subjects in Africa.

Based at the elegant Laikipia River Camp, days unfold with morning, evening, and night safaris, dedicated to tracking and photographing the Black Leopard alongside Laikipia’s extraordinary wildlife. Designed as a small-group expedition, this experience blends exclusivity, expert guiding, and unhurried photography, crafted for travellers drawn to authentic wilderness and the rarest of encounters.

Today, guests arrive in Nairobi by morning. We will then pickup any guests who have arrived in Nairobi the previous day from their respective hotels and will proceed to Laikipia by road. It takes around 6 hours. As we head North from the Kenyan capital, we will pass through different landscapes and watch as it shifts from lush plains to dry desert-like landscapes.
We arrive in time for lunch, post which we will prepare for our first game drive in the conservancy. At dinner time we will return from the safari before we retire for the night.

Over the next 3 days, we will spend whole days in the conservancy looking for the region’s elusive Black Leopards. Our focus will remain on Giza, one of the resident Black Leopards, while we also look for and photograph other wildlife the region has to offer. The day would start by 5:30 am with a hot cup of coffee or tea followed by a light breakfast.

As the sun rises, we will be out on safari until mid day, returning briefly just to have lunch and back on safari once again. We will conclude our evening safari just before dinner. On of the days, we will also enjoy a bush dinner in the middle of the wilderness and under the stars, an experience entirely worth it.

Today, will be our last morning on safari. Soon after we return from the morning drive, we will check-out and proceed to Nairobi arriving in the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport by 4 pm. Tour concludes
